subject: Staging -> On‑Prem: unexpected BGP advertise + MTU fragmentation causing egress failures
messages:
From: Mountain Bank NOC <network@mountainbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production egress intermittent after staging->on‑prem cutover

Jordan / Vanessa,

We started the staging->on‑prem cutover window at 07:30 PT and immediately observed intermittent failures from several Mountain Bank services to a handful of external SaaS APIs (payment gateway / auth). Symptoms: ~1–2% of sessions fail with TLS handshake timeouts; retries succeed after 1–3s. Traceroute shows ICMP fragmentation / "frag needed" messages when path MTU is probed, but also we see traffic occasionally leaving via an unexpected peer AS (looks like a staging VRF leak into the customer fabric).

Attached: mountanbank_traceroute_1201.txt and pcap-egress-1201.zip (sample of failed TCP handshake and ICMP "frag needed").

What we saw so far:
- traceroute (src: 10.45.3.22) ends with "Frag needed mtu 1400" toward api.partner.example.com
- when fragment needed appears, sessions enter a retry loop and succeed once MSS is negotiated lower (intermittent)
- BGP table from their edge briefly contained an additional /24 learned from our staging layer (we have reasons to suspect an accidental redistribute route on the staging router)

This is impacting a handful of customers (low volume) but the behaviour started exactly at cutover. Can we triage the following urgently?
1) Confirm whether Redwood staging announced any unexpected prefixes to Mountain Bank during cutover.
2) Confirm on‑prem NAT device MTU / MSS clamp settings and whether DF is being preserved through the path.
3) Any security group or ACL changes applied during cutover that might drop fragmented packets / ICMP type 3 code 4?

We appreciate quick help — Alice Li and I are on standby.

— Mountain Bank NOC
Network Operations

Thanks for the detailed capture and traceroute — really helpful. Looping in Karthik (network infra) and Vanessa (private deploy eng) to run concurrent checks. Initial triage plan:

- Karthik: please pull BGP RIB & adj‑RIBs from the staging border at 07:20–08:00 and confirm whether any /24s were advertised unintentionally. If there was a redistribute into BGP during the cutover, capture the exact flows and timestamps.
- Vanessa: can you confirm the NAT device(s) on the customer on‑prem edge — MTU, iptables/snat config, and whether MSS clamp is enabled? Also check CGNAT / ephemeral port exhaustion (unlikely given volume, but worth ruling out).
- Mountain Bank: please keep packet captures (we have your pcap) and confirm whether fragmented packets are being dropped by any middleboxes (firewalls, IPS). If possible, run a tcpdump with DF cleared and with MSS-clamp to compare.

I'll keep the ticket open and coordinate an on‑call bridge if needed. For now, can we get RIB snapshots and the on‑prem NAT config snippets (anonymised) attached?

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Mountain Bank NOC <network@mountainbank.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production egress intermittent after staging->on‑prem cutover

Quick status update from the private deploy side:
- I pulled the on‑prem NAT config (attached nat-config-snippet.txt) — NAT device is running HW offload with MTU 9000 between internal fabric and the NAT box, but the downstream link to the customer edge is 1500. There is no MSS clamp configured on the NAT device.
- I also checked the security group rules in the private control plane: no explicit drop for ICMP type 3 code 4, but we do have an egress policy that restricts large fragmented packets on the staging route table (policy was intended to prevent fragmentation-based evasions). That policy was applied as part of the cutover automation.

Interpretation: two factors likely conspired — accidental /24 advertisement from staging (Karthik please confirm) plus an MTU mismatch without MSS clamp plus an egress policy that rejects DF‑fragmented traffic. When PMTU probes fail (ICMP frag needed blocked by policy or middlebox), clients don't back off MSS and TCP handshakes time out.

Temporary mitigations I recommend now:
1) Turn on MSS clamp to 1400 on the on‑prem NAT device (safe interim).
2) Temporarily relax the egress fragmentation policy for Mountain Bank's staging subnet windowed to the cutover IPs.
3) Revoke any unintended BGP advert if Karthik confirms one was present.

I'm happy to push the NAT change if Mountain Bank gives us permission — otherwise we can provide config lines for their on‑prem team to apply.

Vanessa Ortiz
Private Deploy Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Mountain Bank NOC <network@mountainbank.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 16:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production egress intermittent after staging->on‑prem cutover

Update and remediation summary:
- Confirmed staging router briefly redistributed a local /24 into BGP at 07:33 PT due to a mis‑scoped automation job (log attached to NET ticket). The prefix was withdrawn within ~12 minutes.
- Applied MSS clamp (1400) on the on‑prem NAT box at 10:15 PT (applied with Mountain Bank NOC permission). Command used: iptables --table mangle --append POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1400 (also set equivalent on hardware offload as vendor recommended).
- Relaxed the fragmentation egress policy for the staging subnets at 10:20 PT while we validated.

Post‑change validation: Mountain Bank ran an end‑to‑end test suite from affected services — no TLS handshake timeouts observed in a 3 hour window; traceroute no longer shows stray "frag needed" messages and traffic is stable. We still recommend a 48h watch window.

Action items / follow‑ups:
1) Jordan: coordinate a short postmortem with Mountain Bank to review the automation job that redistributed the prefix and add a safety check to the staging deploy pipeline.
2) Vanessa: propose a change to the fragmentation policy to allow ICMP type 3 code 4 for PMTU probes from customer subnets, or implement targeted exceptions.
3) Karthik: will prepare a note with exact commands and vendor offload steps for the on‑prem NAT configuration. I'll attach it to NET-4821.

Thanks everyone for the quick triage. Leaving ticket open until Jordan confirms customer is comfortable to close.

--
Karthik Iyer
Staff Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
